dimension_justifications.soundness: The paper gives a coherent, carefully scoped ownership-receipt contract, a precise normalized-storage interval rule (Eqs. 2-3, PDF p.16), a four-cell factorial, selected independent operator checks, and targeted mutants. Its empirical conclusions are appropriately conditional. However, the core witnesses remain producer-captured receipts and digests; compiled dispatch/autotuning is unbound, most tensor contents are not available in full, and independent numerical validation is limited to eight attention rows and four post-normalization GDN transitions.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The manuscript is unusually explicit about evidence tiers, denominators, and exclusions, with useful contract tables (Tables 4-5 and 15). Figures 1-3 clearly communicate the setup. Nevertheless, the paper is very dense, introduces many non-pooled auxiliary cohorts, and repeatedly uses terms such as "full" in a specialized receipt-completeness sense that remains easy to overread despite the accompanying caveats.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The integration of phase-aware KV/GDN ownership witnesses, receipt replay, and a predeclared fault map is a useful systems-audit framing for hybrid LLM state. The paper itself establishes that the ingredients are established (Tables 9-10, PDF p.18), and the demonstrated scope is one frozen sequential configuration, so the novelty and likely broad impact are meaningful but incremental rather than a major algorithmic or systems advance.

paper_summary: ForkAudit proposes a receipt-bound audit contract for hybrid LLM request forks, separating immutable document KV from recurrent GDN state and requiring lifecycle, storage, dispatch, semantic, and fault-map receipts. On Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, it reports exact registered cross-cell and cross-fan-out equality over 96 configurations, selected dense-FP32 attention and NumPy GDN checks, nine targeted live-fault detections, and allocator differences between full-copy and shared-document KV (Sections 3-5, PDF pp.3-9). The paper explicitly confines these results to conditional receipt-level ownership evidence rather than end-to-end correctness, independent recapture, concurrent serving, or capacity claims.
strongest_verified_contribution: Within its explicitly trusted-capture boundary, the strongest contribution is the operationalized lifecycle/storage audit: Table 5 (PDF p.15) maps seven ownership-contract targets to required receipts, while the primary factorial reports phase-specific request/base and request/peer disjointness, canonical semantic equality, and 288 adjacent-fan-out comparisons (Section 5.3, PDF p.8).
strengths: The contract separates logical state, allocated pages, allocator counters, and unmeasured process/service capacity instead of conflating memory-saving denominators (Section 4.4, PDF p.6; Table 6, PDF p.16).

The paper makes its principal limitations prominent: relational equality is not an independent oracle; selected oracles are not end-to-end; and the schedule is sequential on one CUDA stream (Sections 3, 4.3, and 6, PDF pp.4, 6, 9).
The four-cell KV-by-GDN factorial and phase witnesses directly target the hybrid-state aliasing failure mode rather than relying solely on output equality (Sections 4.1-4.2 and 5.3, PDF pp.5, 8).
Positive controls are mapped to concrete gates and reported separately from detection-rate claims (Table 7 and surrounding text, PDF p.17).
The paper avoids pooling incomparable deployment, HYPIC, serving-framework, and policy cohorts, and labels their authorized inferences (Table 4, PDF p.14; Tables 11-14, PDF pp.19-20).
questions: Can the authors provide an independently produced recapture of the primary receipt stream, rather than replay of producer-generated records, while maintaining the same target predicates?

Can the dispatch evidence be strengthened to bind each relevant call to a compiled binary/version and selected autotuning configuration, rather than only the Python callable and four cache artifacts (Table 5, PDF p.15; Appendix I, PDF p.23)?

How often does the contract identify faults outside the nine hand-designed mutants and four seeded recurrence faults, particularly under concurrent kernels, continuous batching, multiple documents, and different hybrid runtimes?

Does the receipt schema remain practical and informative for a second hybrid architecture and different KV precision/page geometry, rather than only the Q16, 128-token-page Qwen configuration in Table 3 (PDF p.13)?

issues.location: Sections 3-4.3, PDF pp.4-6; Table 5, PDF p.15; Appendix I, PDF p.23.
issues.observed_evidence: The paper says that a full target means receipt completeness only conditional on honest capture and external byte bindings; it cannot independently recapture the producer or reconstruct unarchived device tensors. It also labels dispatch provenance partial because no per-call compiled-binary or autotuning-choice binding exists.
issues.why_it_matters: The receipts can establish consistency of the captured record, but this leaves a gap between the recorded ownership/dispatch view and the behavior of the executing runtime or kernel. This is especially consequential for an audit whose central goal is evidence of isolation rather than merely output agreement.
issues.required_fix: Add an independently provisioned recapture of the primary traces and bind the selected dispatch path to concrete compiled-binary and autotuning identities. Archive enough raw, independently inspectable sampled state to validate storage and semantic predicates without relying on the original producer's sidecars.
issues.verification_test: A separate evaluator must regenerate the records from a clean environment and independently recompute the storage-disjointness, prefix-immutability, cross-arm, and selected numerical predicates; any binary, dispatch, or record mismatch must be reported as a failure rather than reconciled post hoc.
issues.evidence_needed: Independent capture logs, binary/autotuning attestations, raw sampled tensor/state artifacts, and a third-party recapture report for the full 96-cell primary protocol.

issues.location: Section 4.1, PDF p.5; Table 3, PDF p.13; Section 6, PDF p.9; Appendix I, PDF p.23.
issues.observed_evidence: The main evidence covers one Qwen3.5 configuration on one H20 family, BF16/Q16 KV, one 4,095-token partial-tail geometry, N in {1,8,32}, eight PG-19 training books, and sequential round-major execution on one CUDA stream. The eight ranks are explicitly workloads rather than stochastic replicates, and the paper excludes continuous/ragged batching, eviction, multi-document serving, and concurrent kernels.
issues.why_it_matters: The method is presented as an audit contract for hybrid LLM forks, but the visible validation does not establish that its receipts, range rules, or fault sensitivity transfer to other hybrid architectures, runtimes, scheduling regimes, or lower-precision state. The paper's narrow claim framing prevents overclaiming but does not by itself demonstrate broad practical significance.
issues.required_fix: Evaluate the full contract on at least one additional hybrid model/runtime and several materially different lifecycles: concurrent/continuous batching, more than one document, additional page and tail geometries, and lower-precision KV. Include repeated runs where timing or allocator claims are retained.
issues.verification_test: For each added environment, preregister the same target-to-record requirements and show independent replay plus results for clean executions and a held-out fault set; report any targets that become partial or open.
issues.evidence_needed: Multi-model and multi-runtime primary-style audit results, concurrency-aware traces, non-Q16/page-size sweeps, and repeated measurement data for retained quantitative memory claims.

issues.location: Sections 3 and 5.4-5.5, PDF pp.4, 9; Tables 19-20, PDF p.22; Appendix I, PDF p.23.
issues.observed_evidence: The independent attention check covers eight preselected post-RoPE rows, while the GDN oracle covers four layers and begins after the native q/k normalization boundary. The live-fault campaign has nine intended mutants, and the paper correctly says these are positive controls rather than a detector-rate or completeness result.
issues.why_it_matters: These checks corroborate selected internal boundaries but leave broad semantic correctness and fault sensitivity unmeasured. Because the manuscript contains many successful gate and oracle reports, readers can still overestimate how much of the execution path has independent support.
issues.required_fix: Make the main-result hierarchy more visually prominent and add broader, randomly sampled or held-out operator rows and a fault-suite coverage study. Clearly separate contract-target closure from supporting oracle and fault outcomes wherever a "full" status is shown.
issues.verification_test: Evaluate a preregistered held-out set of attention/GDN rows and faults not used to construct the contract, report detection failures as well as successes, and show that target status remains distinct from independent numerical coverage.
issues.evidence_needed: Held-out sampled raw operator sidecars, expanded oracle results across layers/positions, and a documented fault taxonomy with observed detection and escape counts.

llm_usage_disclosure: I am an LLM reviewer. This review used PDF-only access to the frozen submission and did not inspect repositories, artifacts, prior reviews, or external sources.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: An independent, clean-environment recapture that verifies the primary 96-cell ownership predicates and binds actual compiled dispatch behavior.
Primary-style results on additional hybrid architectures/runtimes, concurrent or continuous-batching schedules, multiple documents, and varied KV precisions/page geometries.
A preregistered held-out numerical and fault-coverage evaluation showing where the contract detects and misses defects, with raw sidecars sufficient for independent checking.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: A failed independent recapture, inconsistent raw artifact, or discovery that ownership/disjointness depends on unrecorded pointer, binary, or scheduler state.
Any cross-cell, cross-fan-out, prefix-immutability, or selected-oracle mismatch under the stated frozen protocol.
Evidence that a reported mutation was not live, its clean control failed, or claimed memory comparisons mix the explicitly separated denominators.
